sections.html:
Bills come from the Lenoir County Tax Department in the administration building at 101 North Queen Street in Kinston. The phone is 252-527-7174, and the office is open weekdays from 8:30 to 5:00.

One office carries several jobs. It lists and appraises real estate, keeps ownership and transfer records, tracks exemptions, exclusions and deferrals, and mails the bills. It also bills the special districts layered over the county: fire districts, municipal service districts and drainage districts. Solid waste fees, privilege licenses and permits to move mobile homes run through the same counter.

The county website links to online bill viewing and payment, real property records, GIS maps, a scheduler for real property appeals, and listing forms for business and individual personal property. If you are selling, check the bill there first and then phone for a payoff figure.

September 1 is the due date, yet nothing extra is charged until January 6. From then, interest is 2 percent through February 1 and 3/4 percent per month after that, and a partial month counts as a full one. For mailed payments the postmark sets the date.

Dates that shape a Lenoir County tax year
StepWhat the law saysStatute
ListingBegins on the first business day in January and ends January 31G.S. 105-307
Payment dateSeptember 1 of the fiscal year the tax is levied forG.S. 105-360
Last interest-free dayThe day before January 6G.S. 105-360
Review board convenesOpens its first meeting sometime from the first Monday in April to the first Monday in MayG.S. 105-322
Next appeal levelNotice of appeal in writing to the state commission, filed within a month after the ruling is mailedG.S. 105-290

The Board of Equalization and Review decides real estate appeals. It meets in the spring and adjourns in April. Your next chance comes when the 2027 window opens on January 1, 2027.

Under G.S. 105-322 this quasi-judicial board hears disputes about how real estate and personal property were listed and appraised, and about exemption applications, exclusion requests and present-use classifications.

The deadlines are firm. Request a hearing by letter or in person before the board adjourns, and expect a written decision within 30 days after adjournment. If you are still unhappy, file notice with the state Property Tax Commission inside 30 days of the mailing date, stating your grounds and sending a copy to the assessor. The county site offers a form for scheduling a real property appeal.

Values were reset by a reappraisal effective January 1, 2025, following the one effective January 1, 2017. North Carolina law sets the outside limit at eight years between reappraisals of real property.

In between, a value changes only when the property does, for example through new construction or a removed building. During a reappraisal, certified appraisers visit parcels, confirm characteristics and study sales and costs so every property is measured as of the same date.

Treat the assessed figure as a tax number and not a market price. Weigh it against recent sales when choosing an asking price, and ask the office for the current assessed value on your parcel.

Kinston's tax office handles the AV-9 form for North Carolina's three homestead breaks. Pick whichever fits, because you cannot stack them. Filing belongs in the January listing period, but the county will still take an application until June 1 of the tax year.

  • Age or disability: shields $25,000 of value or half the appraised value, whichever is greater. You must be 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, with 2026 income at or under $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: takes $45,000 off the appraised value. Neither age nor income matters. Send Form NCDVA-9 through the assessor.
  • Circuit breaker: holds your bill to 4.0 percent of income if income is at or below the limit, or 5.0 percent if it lands between the limit and 150 percent of it. The 2026 limit is $58,200. You need five years of owning and living in the house and a new application every year, and the deferred tax comes due on a sale.

Land used for farming, horticulture or forestry can qualify for present-use value, which lowers the assessment. Lenoir County has an AV-7 form that requests an estimate of deferred taxes, a smart step before selling such land.

sections.h2: What landlords and business owners must list
sections.html:
Anyone holding personal property tied to a business or other income-producing use must file a Business Personal Property Listing Form during January. Examples include machinery, equipment, computers, furniture, fixtures, farm machinery, airplanes, supplies and construction in progress. Rental owners who keep appliances, tools or equipment for their Lenoir County units should read that list.

An account that listed last year receives its form in the mail automatically. If none arrives, ask for one during regular office hours. Organizations seeking an exemption from personal property tax must file their application by January 31.

Before December ends, the tax office also mails abstract listings to every taxpayer who listed the year before. To list real estate for the first time, such as a newly built house, call the Tax Assessor's Office.

The tax lien attaches to a parcel on January 1 and stays with the house until the balance is paid. For a sale, the attorney or title company normally asks the Lenoir County Tax Department for the amount and pays it from the seller's proceeds.

Personal property is treated differently. An unpaid personal property bill can become a lien on every parcel the taxpayer owns in that taxing unit, which means an old boat or equipment bill can turn up against your house. Boats, jet skis, aircraft, mobile homes and unlicensed vehicles are listed each January, with a 10 percent penalty for a late listing.

Because real estate is on a permanent listing system, you do not have to relist the house annually unless its value changed.

To keep the sale on track, phone 252-527-7174 early and ask what is owed on the parcel and on any personal property account in your name. Hand the closing attorney that number so it shows on the settlement statement. A cash sale skips lender underwriting, but the same balance still gets cleared at closing.

To collect, the county can file a court action that mirrors a mortgage foreclosure, brought where the property is located. Owners of record, spouses and other lienholders receive notice.

The foreclosure sale is a public auction outside the courthouse. The steps after the bidding are short:

  • A bidder may be asked to put down as much as 20 percent.
  • The commissioner files a report on the sale within three days.
  • Ten days run from the report for anyone to object or raise the bid.
  • A fee of up to 5 percent of the price goes to the commissioner.
  • Before a judge confirms the sale, redemption is possible for whoever pays everything owed on the parcel.

If a foreclosure notice reaches you, call the tax office and a legal aid provider right away.

sections.h2: Checklist before you list a Kinston-area house
sections.html:
A few calls to the Lenoir County Tax Department can save a closing from stalling. Work through these before you accept an offer:

  1. Look up the parcel on the county site and confirm the owner name matches the deed.
  2. Ask whether any special district, such as a fire, municipal service or drainage district, adds a separate charge to the bill.
  3. Ask about any deferred tax if the land has present-use value.
  4. Find out whether a boat, aircraft, mobile home or unlicensed vehicle in your name is still unlisted or unpaid.
  5. Request the payoff figure in writing for the settlement.

None of this costs anything, and each answer is one fewer surprise for the buyer's attorney.

Lenoir County has about 55,837 residents, down from 59,495 in 2010, and 27,402 housing units across 399.09 square miles. The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $120,500, owners live in 59.2 percent of homes, and median rent is $861. Median household income is $45,143. At these home values a tax bill is a real share of yearly housing cost, and back taxes can eat much of a house's equity. Only 131 building permits were issued in 2025, so a resale competes mainly with other older houses.

faqs.q: Which phone number reaches Lenoir County tax staff?
faqs.a: Dial 252-527-7174. The office is at 101 North Queen Street in Kinston and keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 5:00.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Lenoir County real estate value?
faqs.a: Appeals go to the Board of Equalization and Review, which adjourns in April. The window for 2027 opens January 1, 2027.

faqs.q: Must a Lenoir County homeowner list the house each year?
faqs.a: No. Real estate is on a permanent listing system, so a house is relisted only after a change in value. Boats, aircraft and unlicensed vehicles need a January listing.

faqs.q: What does a late personal property listing cost in Lenoir County?
faqs.a: A 10 percent penalty. Listings made after the period ending January 31 are charged it.

faqs.q: Can a house with unpaid Lenoir County tax be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing pays the balance out of your proceeds. Get the figure from the tax office before you sign so it appears on the settlement statement.
